newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Foreign investors boost trade in Zimbabwe stocks.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investors boost trade in Zimbabwe stocks.

text.p: Foreign investors returned to Zimbabwe's Stock Exchange (ZSE) in a big way on Monday after watching trade from the sidelines for most of last week, and some brokers predicted they would play hard and long in a market seen bullish for at least three months.
"The character of the market must keep quite a number of these (foreign) players here for quite some time," one broker said.
With good rains, the southern African country's agriculture- based economy is expected to grow by seven percent next year from an estimated five percent in 1996.
On Monday, the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange's main 57-counter industrial index dropped 55.23 points to close at 8,061.76.
Although gains were recorded in several stocks, including heavyweight Zimbabwe Newspapers, 100 cents higher at 2,500, and Tobacco Sales Limited (TSL), 30 cents up at 650.
Brokers said the market volume was boosted by retail and hotel group Meikles where 2.6 million shares changed hands at a special bargain of 2,200 -- 400 cents lower than the opening price.
Gold producer Falgold traded five cents to 95, and the seven-counter mining index ended 2.39 points lower at 1,196.87.
